scenarios.title: Core opposition, with outside support
scenarios.agenda: Explore the draft and October 7 inquiry as possible common ground. These roles are hypothetical; no agreement is asserted.
obstacles: Universal military or civilian service is supported by core opposition answers, while Ra'am opposes requiring Arab citizens to perform either. What service policy would an outside supporter accept?
Recorded partner pledges restrict some cabinet combinations. A refusal to join is not automatically a promise to abstain or provide outside support.
scenarios.leadership: A premier and any rotation deal would need agreement. Poll rank does not legally appoint a prime minister, and this scenario supplies no agreed rotation.
scenarios.source: Party answers, Ynet, Sep 16, 2026; recorded pledges shown below

scenarios.title: Core opposition, with a Haredi partner
scenarios.agenda: Test whether an added cabinet partner closes the seat gap and how its policy requirements change the bargain. This is a hypothetical combination.
obstacles: Core opposition answers favor military or civilian service for all; Shas distinguishes students who remain in yeshiva from those who leave. A shared draft bill would have to resolve that difference.

Civil marriage is supported in the core parties' recorded positions, while the source summary says Shas opposes civil alternatives. That requires a specific compromise, not a claim that all religion policy agrees.
scenarios.leadership: Leadership, ministry allocation and the order of passing any prerequisite law remain unagreed. Adding seats does not settle these terms.
scenarios.source: Ynet draft questionnaire, Sep 16, 2026; Jerusalem Post religion/state summary, Sep 10, 2026

scenarios.title: Netanyahu-led parties
scenarios.agenda: Test the selected poll's seat majority, then inspect the parties' recorded terms. This is a hypothetical post-election arrangement, not a coalition agreement.
obstacles: Shas accepts enlistment of students who leave yeshiva; UTJ's reported answer continues to oppose their enlistment. Coalition membership does not erase this draft-law dispute.

Religious Zionism's court answer includes a 61-vote override; Otzma gave no detailed court platform in the same questionnaire. Missing evidence cannot establish coalition-wide agreement on that mechanism.
scenarios.leadership: Netanyahu is the scenario's proposed premier. Appointment still requires the legal formation process and an initial confidence vote; ministries and written terms are not supplied here.
scenarios.source: Ynet draft questionnaire, Sep 16, 2026; courts questionnaire, Sep 22, 2026

historical.title: Outside support has a history
historical.text: Rabin's 1992 coalition began with 62 seats. After Shas left in September 1993, it had 56 and relied on outside support from Arab factions. Cabinet seats and parliamentary backing were different quantities.
